summary: Cape George Harbour light on Bras d'Or Lake was first lit in 1875; its present wooden tower dates from 1950, and the Murray family kept the light for 94 years.

light.characteristic: Fl W 4s (seasonal, per the Coast Guard list)

structures.note: erected sometime between 2012 and 2014, beside the wooden tower

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory). Two guides give different approaches: a walk of about 1 km from Oldys Road, or a short walk from a campground car park off NS 4.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (per LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory); the 2020 announcement says a non-federal owner now manages it, unnamed

events.note: Original light established; first keeper Norman Murray from 3 August 1875
Present square wooden tower completed March 1950 (contract 1949, H. E. McDonald)
Lamp changed from oil to an electric bulb on ten batteries
Declared fully automated; the Murray family had kept the light for 94 years
Dwelling, barn and oil store declared surplus; a former keeper bought them and removed them from the site (LighthouseFriends)
Skeletal tower carrying a light erected beside the wooden tower, between 2012 and 2014
Lighthouse Directory: 'Inactive since 2013 (?)' for the old tower; the Coast Guard list still shows a seasonal light (see notes_for_editor)
Designated under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act; announced 29 October 2020

keepers.name: John Murray
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends says he 'served for thirty years' although its dates run 1882 to 1922; keepers' list 1903 places Murray, John at Cape George, Great Bras d'Or Lake (matched by row on scan 231, printed p. 218; the row was checked on the page image at screen resolution)

keepers.note: Served 39 years until automation; LighthouseFriends says he bought the surplus dwelling buildings in 1975. Not the 'Munroe, William L' listed at Three Top Island in the 1903 table.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station record lists 1950 and 1875 for different values. Parks Canada and LighthouseFriends agree the light was first established in 1875 and the present wooden tower dates from 1950; a 1950 start date describes the present tower only.

notes_for_editor: Ownership is disputed: LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse (visitor section) and, in its 2020 paragraph, that a new, non-federal owner manages it; the Lighthouse Directory names the Canadian Coast Guard as owner and site manager; the 2020 Parks Canada announcement lists the lighthouse among those managed by new, non-federal owners without naming them. Status is disputed: the Lighthouse Directory says 'Inactive since 2013 (?)' for the old tower and describes the active light on a skeletal tower; the current Coast Guard list shows Fl W 4s marked seasonal. The station record carries 'active' (from the Coast Guard list) and a 2013 deactivation (from the directory); the two conflict. LighthouseFriends says John Murray 'served for thirty years' while its own dates span 1882 to 1922 (forty years); the story quotes both. The 1903 keepers' list was read as an OCR table and matched by row: 'Murray, John' against 'Cape George, Great Bras d'Or Lake' (scan 231, printed p. 218, 1904v38i8p21_0209). The page image was viewed at screen resolution (not magnified) and the row looked aligned. The 1915 keepers' table (1916v51i17p21_1196) prints 'John Murray Nov 3, 1882' on printed p. 71 (scan 78), in the Nova Scotia station list for Medway to Salter head; 'Cape George' is not on that page (the 1915 entry is 'George, cape' on printed p. 69). The 1915 row is therefore not linked to Cape George and was dropped from the story and from the roster. Do not confuse with 'Munroe, William L', who sits at Three Top Island in the same 1903 table. The Department 'Cape George' entries of 1908 and 1909 (1909v43i12p21_0579 scan 76; 1910v44i11p21_0659 scan 77) are the Antigonish County light on the Northumberland Strait (record ca-ns-cape-george, lat 45.87, lon -61.90), a different station, and were excluded. The 1874 announcement and the 1875 construction details rest on LighthouseFriends alone; the pre-1900 Department reports are not in the corpus. No storm, wreck or rescue at this station is sourced, so there is no storms chapter. Excluded: novascotiavacation.ca (contradicts the automation year, gives 1973, and says the 1875 tower is no longer standing); MarineRadar (aggregator). The Duncan McRae found in search results (a Manitoba stonemason, 1813-1898) is a different man. Search budget: four websearch.py calls, one more than the guide's three.
